content: In which land did Job, the blameless and upright man, live?
explanation: He feared God and shunned evil. “There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job.” (Job 1:1, BSB)

content: How does the Bible describe Job before his troubles began?
explanation: He feared God. “And this man was blameless and upright, fearing God and shunning evil.” (Job 1:1, BSB)

content: Before his troubles, how many sons and daughters did Job have?
explanation: He was greatly blessed. “He had seven sons and three daughters” (Job 1:2, BSB)

content: After losing everything, what did Job say about the LORD?
options: The LORD gave and has taken
explanation: He still blessed God's name. “The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the name of the LORD.” (Job 1:21, BSB)

content: In all his early losses, what did Job not do?
explanation: He stayed faithful. “In all this, Job did not sin or charge God with wrongdoing.” (Job 1:22, BSB)

content: After losing his family and wealth, what covered Job's body?
explanation: From his feet to his head. “and infected Job with terrible boils from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head.” (Job 2:7, BSB)

content: When Job's three friends first came, how long did they sit with him silently?
explanation: They saw his great suffering. “Then they sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights, but no one spoke a word to him” (Job 2:13, BSB)

content: How did the LORD finally answer Job?
explanation: God spoke to Job directly. “Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind” (Job 38:1, BSB)

content: At the end of Job's story, how much did the LORD give him?
explanation: This came after he prayed for his friends. “the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions.” (Job 42:10, BSB)

content: What did the LORD say about Job to Satan?
options: No one on earth is like him
explanation: Job was blameless and upright. “For there is no one on earth like him” (Job 1:8, BSB)

content: When God let Satan test Job, what could Satan not touch at first?
explanation: God set limits. “but you must not lay a hand on the man himself.” (Job 1:12, BSB)

content: After hearing all his losses, what did Job do after tearing his robe?
explanation: He still honored God. “He fell to the ground and worshiped” (Job 1:20, BSB)

content: What struck the house where Job's children were eating?
explanation: It came from the desert. “when suddenly a mighty wind swept in from the desert and struck the four corners of the house.” (Job 1:19, BSB)

content: Who told suffering Job, “Curse God and die!”?
explanation: Job refused. “Then Job’s wife said to him, “Do you still retain your integrity? Curse God and die!”” (Job 2:9, BSB)

content: What did Job ask his wife about accepting from God?
explanation: He did not sin in what he said. “Should we accept from God only good and not adversity?” (Job 2:10, BSB)

content: Sitting among the ashes, what did Job use to scrape his sores?
explanation: He was in great pain. “And Job took a piece of broken pottery to scrape himself as he sat among the ashes.” (Job 2:8, BSB)

content: In his suffering, what did Job say he knows?
explanation: His hope was in God. “But I know that my Redeemer lives” (Job 19:25, BSB)

content: What did God ask Job about the earth's foundations?
explanation: God showed His greatness. “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?” (Job 38:4, BSB)

content: After God spoke to him, what did Job say had changed?
options: Now my eyes have seen You
explanation: He had only heard of God before. “My ears had heard of You, but now my eyes have seen You.” (Job 42:5, BSB)

content: In the book of Job, what is called wisdom?
explanation: Turning from evil is understanding. “Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom” (Job 28:28, BSB)

content: Why was the LORD angry with Job's friends?
explanation: Job had spoken accurately. “For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has.” (Job 42:7, BSB)

content: Which of these was one of Job's three friends?
explanation: The others were Eliphaz and Zophar. “Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite” (Job 2:11, BSB)

content: Before his troubles, how many camels did Job own?
explanation: He also had 7,000 sheep. “and he owned 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels” (Job 1:3, BSB)

content: Which younger man grew angry at Job for justifying himself rather than God?
explanation: He was the son of Barachel. “This kindled the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite” (Job 32:2, BSB)

content: What was the name of Job's first daughter after his restoration?
explanation: The others were Keziah and Keren-happuch. “He named his first daughter Jemimah” (Job 42:14, BSB)

content: How many more years did Job live after his restoration?
explanation: He saw four generations. “After this, Job lived 140 years” (Job 42:16, BSB)

content: God asked Job if he could loosen the belt of which constellation?
explanation: Only God rules the stars. “Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the belt of Orion?” (Job 38:31, BSB)

content: Which raiders took Job's oxen and donkeys?
explanation: Only one servant escaped. “the Sabeans swooped down and took them away.” (Job 1:15, BSB)

content: When Job's family came to comfort him, what did each give him?
explanation: They ate with him in his house. “And each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.” (Job 42:11, BSB)
